out_items.name: Certified Food Protection Manager

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. NO CFM ONSITE AT BEGINNING OF INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program. PLEASE ENSURE MORE STAFF RECEIVE A CERTIFIED FOOD MANAGER CERTIFICATION. PIC UNDERSTANDS A CFM SHOULD BE ONSITE DURING ALL HOURS OF OPERATION.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: OBSERVED RAW SHELLED EGGS STORED ABOVE COOKED CHICKEN IN THE THREE-DOOR PREP-TOP.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC REORGANIZED COOLER DURING INSPECTION AND EHS PROVIDED GUIDANCE.

out_items.name: Proper cooling time and temperature

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety foods are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours: OBSERVED TWO BATCHES OF RICE AT 46-49F AND FRIED SPINACH AT 46F MADE THE NIGHT PRIOR TO INSPECTION IN THE WALK-IN COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. PIC DISCARDED OF FOODS DURING INSPECTION. EHS REITERATED PROPER COOLING METHODS. PLEASE ENSURE ALL STAFF UNDERSTAND PROPER COOLING METHODS TO PREVENT FURTHER ENFORCEMENT ACTION.

violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. PLEASE SEAL ALL HOLES AND GAPS PRESENT ON THE BACK DOOR PRIOR TO THE FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: OBSERVED SOME BOXES OF DRINKS AT THE FRONT BAR AND A CONTAINER OF ONIONS IN THE WALK-IN COOLER STORED ON THE GROUND. OBSERVED TWO BUCKETS OF RICE ON THE FLOOR IN THE BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PLEASE ENSURE ALL FOOD ITEMS ARE ELEVATED OFF THE GROUND TO PREVENT CONTAMINATION AND ALL FOR EASY CLEANING. RICE WAS MOVED DURING INSPECTION. CLAY POT (Inspection Date: 08/27/2026) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing utensils improperly stored between use as follows: OBSERVED MULTIPLE BULK FOOD ITEMS WITH CUPS STORED DIRECTLY IN THE FOOD.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS PROVIDED GUIDANCE. PLEASE ENSURE CORRECTION AS SOON AS POSSIBLE.

violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. PLEASE DISCONTINUE USING THESE CONTAINERS AS THEY ARE NOT NSF-APPROVED OR EQUIVALENT AND ARE NOT MADE TO BE WASHED, RINSED, AND SANITIZED REPEATEDLY.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding

violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. violations.corrective_action: Shell eggs that have not been treated to destroy Salmonella shall be stored in refrigerated equipment that maintains an ambient temperature of 45F or less. PIC DISCARDED OF EGGS DURING INSPECTION AND UNDERSTANDS EGGS SHOULD NEVER BE STORED OUTSIDE WITHOUT TEMPERATURE CONTROL.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: OBSERVED NO DATE MARKING SYSTEM IN PLACE AT ESTABLISHMENT.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC UNDERSTANDS A DATE MARKING SYSTEM SHOULD BE IN PLACE FOR ANY COOKED OR PREPARED FOODS KEPT FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS PLEASE ENSURE CORRECTION BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION. .

violations.corrective_action: Within 30 days, the permit holder shall replace or upgrade the water heater with a unit that meets the following design and capacity requirements: (1) Commercial grade, (2) Minimum of 50 gallon storage tank, (3) Minimum recovery rate of 126gph of 120F water at a 80F rise, and (4) Specifications and installation meet National Sanitation Foundation (NSF) Standard 5. As an option, the permit holder may choose to remove a newly installed warewashing machine to comply with this requirement.
